item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Tue Nov 10, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Evening Compline — Fri Nov 13, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Veteran’s Day Luminary Trail Walk — Wed Nov 11, 5:00 PM — Winters Leadership Memorial
item.description:
Set along the Winters Memorial Trail on Veterans Day, Nov 11, 2026, Mainspring of Ephrata’s Winters Leadership Memorial Committee will continue the tradition they began on Veterans Day 2014 and host a moving Luminary Tribute to those who have served. item.title: Evening Compline — Thu Nov 12, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

item.title: Flamenco y Sol: Flamenco at Its Essence — Fri Nov 13, 7:30 PM — Ware Center for the Arts
item.description:
Flamenco y Sol, in collaboration with Rebeca Tomas and A Palo Seco Flamenco Company, presents an evening of traditional flamenco in its most authentic form, featuring live music, improvisation, and the dynamic interplay between dancer, singer, and guitarist. Rooted in the tablao tradition, the performance highlights the raw emotional power of flamenco through cante (song), baile (dance), and toque (guitar playing). Each moment unfolds organically, offering audiences a direct and immersive experience of this living art form. Through group choreography and solo moments, each artist’s unique voice emerges, creating a powerful and electrifying theatrical experience.
At 6:30 PM, enjoy a pre-show flamenco lecture by Dr. Ana Börger-Greco Presented in partnership with the Skrodinsky Family Foundation.
